subject: 2025 City Council Candidates Forum
overview: Ten candidates for City Council participated in a forum to discuss municipal priorities including zoning reform, infrastructure funding, and fiscal management. The program featured two rounds of questions on resident-submitted topics and concluded with personal closing statements from the candidates.

items.title: Introduction and forum procedures
items.summary: Moderators outlined the forum rules, introduced the participating candidates, and noted absences due to prior commitments or medical recovery.

items.title: Question Round 1: Housing, zoning, and infrastructure
items.summary: Candidates responded to questions regarding gentrification, business district revitalization, developer linkage fees, parking requirements, and police oversight. Discussion also touched on historic preservation, LGBTQ+ community support, and methods for addressing the road repair backlog.

items.title: Question Round 2: Charter reform, municipal finance, and environment
items.summary: Candidates debated the proposed city charter, high school funding, small business support, and the fiscal wisdom of using free cash for operating expenses. Additional topics included municipal divestment from certain industries, tree canopy expansion, and long-term visions for the city's built environment.

items.title: Closing statements
items.summary: Participating candidates delivered two-minute closing remarks summarizing their platforms and experience; Cara Caraviello delivered a statement on behalf of candidate Rick Caraviello.
